subject: How to catch  non-convergence and/or inadmissible estimates (Heywood)

messages.author: c69bf3eeace29d5d
messages.subject: How to catch  non-convergence and/or inadmissible estimates (Heywood)
parts:
Hi Everybody! 

This is the code I previously used to catch convergence problems, with the try commando:

 fitted.j =try(sem(modelstring,data=data.frame(X.j)))
      if (class(fitted) == "try-error"){
        cat("Some problem with i=", i )
       
        next
      }

However,maybe due to updates in the sofware this does not work properly:
> fitted.j
** WARNING ** lavaan (0.5-11) did NOT converge after 18 iterations
** WARNING ** Estimates below are most likely unreliable

  Number of observations                         10000

  Estimator                                         ML
  Minimum Function Test Statistic                   NA
  Degrees of freedom                                NA
  P-value (Unknown)                                 NA

> class(fitted.j)== "try-error"
[1] FALSE

So the try command did not catch the non-convergence. 

Has anyone a better code to offer, that will catch these kinds of problems?

Best, Njål

messages.author: 89c9fc822e34b78c
messages.subject: Re: How to catch  non-convergence and/or inadmissible estimates (Heywood)
parts:
> So the try command did not catch the non-convergence.
>
> Has anyone a better code to offer, that will catch these kinds of problems?

inspect(fit, "converged")

returns TRUE/FALSE.

If only I had documented that somewhere.

Yves.
